av_event.line_text: A daughter. Fifteen. She's with me every other weekend and one night a week. The rest of the time it's quiet.
av_event.what: As he says it, Craig briefly turns his head over his left shoulder towards the framed photo of the teenage girl on the bookshelf behind him, holds the look for a second or two, then turns back to the screen with his face unchanged.

text:
B: Hello? Right, I can see you. Darren.
A: Hi, Darren. Craig.
B: Alright. Third one of these now. Getting the hang of it, sort of.
A: Ja, same. They go quickly.
B: They do. Where are you, then? You don't sound local to anywhere I know.
A: Woodley. Near Reading. Originally Durban, South Africa, but I've been here twenty-four years.
B: Oh, right. I'm Castleford, West Yorkshire. I've hardly been further south than Leicester. What do you do?
A: Structural engineer. Mostly refurbishment. Old buildings, people wanting walls taken out, that sort of thing.
B: Ha. So you're the bloke who says whether we can knock through. I'm a joiner. Housing association, all the social housing round Wakefield. Doors, windows, kitchens, floorboards, boarding up after break-ins.
A: So you're the one who actually does it.
B: Somebody has to. No offence, but half the drawings we get, you look at them and think, has this fella ever stood in a house?
A: None taken. I review contractor drawings. I think the same about some of those.
B: Ha! Fair enough. It's the uPVC frames that get me, though. Whoever designed them wants a word.
A: Er, what's the problem with them?
B: They're cheap, that's the problem. Hinges go, the door drops, it won't lock, tenant rings up, and I'm the one stood there in the rain with a screwdriver because the scheduling system's sent me to the wrong end of Normanton first. Sorry, I'm just being a grump.
A: No, that's fair. We had a new software rollout in March. Changed everything for no reason. Took me a month to get back to where I was.
B: Always the way, that. Do they ask the people who actually use it? Do they heck.
A: No. They don't.
B: You into your rugby? I saw a Springboks mug on your shelf.
A: Ja. I watch every test. Not sure the squad's that good this year, mind.
B: Union, though. Well, nobody's perfect. I'm league. Cas Tigers. Lost again Sunday.
A: Sorry to hear that.
B: Ref were a disgrace. Anyway. What else do you do, when you're not doing your sums?
A: Cycle. Weekend mornings, on my own. Same few loops out towards Wargrave and Henley. And I make biltong in the garage. Dried meat.
B: Oh, I know biltong. Lad at work brought some in once. Proper good, that. You make it yourself?
A: I built a drying box. Light bulb and a computer fan, basically. This batch is nearly done.
B: That's grand, that. I've got a shed, I make bits out of offcuts. Bird boxes and that. Built me sister a bench for her garden last year.
A: That's good. Nice to make something you can actually use.
B: That's it, yeah. Have you got family down there? Kids?
A: A daughter. Fifteen. She's with me every other weekend and one night a week. The rest of the time it's quiet.
B: Yeah. I know quiet. I live on me own an' all. You end up talking to next door's cat, do you know what I mean.
A: Ja. Or the TV.
B: Or that. Mind you, I've been meaning to sort me guttering since October, so I've got plenty to be getting on with if I could be bothered.
A: Mine needs doing too. It's been on the list since—
